answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to post a refundable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. A new identity therefore has no trusted signal merely because it is cheap to create: it must lock real value and risk losing it. Spreading attacks across many accounts multiplies the capital tied up, while a pearl-sized stake per account can still deter mass Sybils if audits are hard to predict and rewards for cheating are smaller than expected losses. A pigment badge alone would not provide this security.
